correctness.rationale: Right translations have the explicitly derived two-coset 2x2 Fourier blocks with singular values |r|+|t| and ||r|-|t||. Odd group order makes r,t nonzero. Vanishing occurs exactly at the dual annihilators of u-v and u+v; inclusion-exclusion gives the complete general nullity. Over F_p^d, linear dependence yields exactly three strata; signed-difference-class counting gives all support multiplicities. For independent differences, character values fill a p-by-p root grid uniformly; strictly increasing gaps in 2cos(pi*j/p) and a lower bound on plus modes give smallest positive singular value 2(1-cos(pi/p)), multiplicity 4p^(d-2), and norm 4. The proof verifies all quantifiers and p=3 boundary. Standalone checker constructs direct group convolution matrices, checks modular ranks and numerical singular lists, and exhausts two small complete censuses; finite checks are not relied on to prove the infinite theorem.

originality.rationale: The claimed contribution is the all-balanced-support arithmetic nullity and exact three-class support census for F_p^d, plus the optimized positive singular endpoint and its exact multiplicity and quadratic conditioning. The two-coset block method and generic representation-theoretic Cayley characteristic polynomials are acknowledged as prior. Full available primary treatments and the nearest published three-tap claim address different support sizes/invariants and do not state the combined balanced-four-tap conclusions; a broad historical implication remains possible.
residual_risks: The representation-theoretic two-coset reduction is standard, and an older general formula for Cayley operator singular values or mixed two-two supports could subsume the claimed results; bounded primary-source searching cannot exclude this.

value.rationale: Two translations in each coset are a natural first genuinely balanced four-move sampling or averaging family on generalized dihedral groups. The theorem fully quantifies recoverability for all balanced supports, counts every support by its exact kernel size, and gives a sharp smallest-positive spectral value and p^2 stability loss for the dominant independent regime. It is an infinite-family complete classification with nontrivial arithmetic and spectral endpoint analysis rather than a computational toy or an arbitrary parameter substitution.
